question.text: As per the workbook example, an investor saving Rs.5,322 per month and earning 10% p.a. instead of the planned 12% p.a. over 25 years would accumulate a corpus of approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (NISM Series XVII, p.89), the illustration uses a 25-year horizon with monthly savings of Rs.5,322 and an effective return of 10% (instead of the planned 12%), yielding a corpus of approximately Rs.70 lakh. The Trap: A 2 percentage point shortfall in annual returns appears small but compounds substantially over a 25-year horizon — the impact is far greater than a linear estimate would suggest. Note: Build a buffer into retirement plans — for example, if the client needs Rs.1 crore, plan toward a stretch target so that minor return shortfalls do not derail the goal.
